# Rarebert agent guide

## Scratch and temporary work

Prefer `.opencode/system/` for any temporary or scratch work — intermediate
files, drafts, notes, captured output, partial diffs, anything disposable.
Treat it as the project's private `/tmp`: create subdirectories freely, never
commit anything under it, and clean up your own scratch files when a task is
done unless asked to keep them.

Do not write scratch files to the project root, `lib/`, `scripts/`, `src/`,
or `system/`. Use `.opencode/system/` exclusively for ephemeral output.

## Generated Makefile — do not edit directly

The root `Makefile` is **generated by the project** via `make reload`
(`scripts/reload.ts` → `lib/runtime/makefile.ts#refreshMakefile`). Never write to
it by hand: any hand-added target is silently dropped on the next reload.

> **2026-10-23 status:** the `Makefile` is currently stale (targets call the
> removed `node index.js`) and `reload.ts` is a stub pending reimplementation —
> do not run `make` targets until the generator is rebuilt.

- One `bun launch.ts <name>` target per discovered `scripts/` module is
  generated automatically.
- Non-module targets (`deps`, `test`) live in the `EXTRA_TARGETS` template
  inside `lib/runtime/makefile.ts`.
- To add or change a target: scaffold a `scripts/` module or edit
  `EXTRA_TARGETS`, then run `make reload` and commit
  the regenerated file.

See `docs/modules.md` → "The Generated Makefile" for the full specification.

## Memo system usage

Memos are local-only sidecar files (`<file>.`) managed through the memo
CLI. **`bun launch.ts memo --help` is the authoritative interface reference**
— consult it before any mutating memo operation.

Print with `bun launch.ts memo [files...]`. Targeted inspection and
disposal:

- `bun launch.ts memo --oldest` — prints the **most-forgotten** memo: the
  one that would be printed first by the DAG print (most deeply included
  module in the walk order, oldest memo within it). Non-mutating; run this
  first to see what disposal would affect.
- `bun launch.ts memo --forget --oldest` — drops exactly that one memo. No
  module reference required; the whole-project DAG is computed the same
  way as `--oldest`.

**Be very careful when performing stale memo disposal.** Memos encode
hard-won context; a dropped memo is gone (sidecars are gitignored, so git
cannot recover it — only `--commit` snapshots in git notes can). Before
disposing: run `bun launch.ts memo --oldest` and/or a scoped print to
confirm the memo is genuinely stale, prefer the narrowest tool (`--forget
--oldest` drops one memo; `--forget <module>` wipes a whole sidecar; `--drop
<module> <indices>` targets specific entries), and never bulk-forget to
"clean up" without reading what is being dropped.

Convention — **one key memo + simple references**:

- Attach a memo **once**, to the **key module**: the trouble maker (where
  the problem lives) or the most troubled module (most affected).
- Duplicate memo text across multiple modules **only** when the text is
  simple and **references** the related memo, e.g.
  `SLIMMING: see the key SLIMMING DIRECTIVE memo on scripts/analyze.ts — ...`.
- Never paste the same verbose memo verbatim into many sidecars — updates
  would have to be repeated N times and the corpus becomes noise.
- Diagnostic memos (`unused-import:`, `broken-import:`, ...) are
  transient: drop them once the underlying issue is fixed.

## Module authoring specification

Authoritative spec for every runnable module in `scripts/` (and for TUI/flow
submodules). A fresh-context implementer should read this top to bottom
before implementing a scaffolded module — the scaffold templates
(`lib/runtime/libs.ts`)
references these rules inline. Where older sections below conflict, this
section wins.

### Module shapes and the export contract

- **CLI** (default): `export default new CLI('<name>.ts', main, meta);` —
  plus `export { main, meta };` (`.supportsDirectRunning()` is deprecated
  and a no-op — direct execution was retired with the Bunli entry)
- **TUI**: same shape with `new TUI(...)` — full-screen interactive modules
- **Flows**: a main may return `exit(Interface.createInterface('<name>')
.stage(a).stage(b))` — stages are themselves TUI submodules

### meta contract (data-driven; the zod parse engine owns parsing)

- Metas are declared with `defineMeta({...})` (exported from
  `lib/runtime/CLI.ts` and the barrel) — the generic-`const` modifier keeps
  flag string literals narrow so `OptsOf<typeof meta>` / `Args<typeof meta>`
  derive real typed keys. A plain `satisfies ModuleMeta` widens the flag
  literals and collapses the derived opts object into an index signature.
- `name` / `description` / `usage` — rendered into `--help`
- `options` — declared flags; the zod-backed engine in `lib/runtime/CLI.ts`
  parses them with Commander parity (`typeParser` supports
  int / float / array / choices)
- `args` — positional declarations `[{ name, required, description }]`.
  **The engine owns required-argument checking** — never hand-validate
  positionals
- `allowUnknownOption: true` — unknown flags/values stay VERBATIM in
  `positional` (memo's ACTIONS dispatch depends on this)

### main callback contract

- Signature `async function main(args: Args<typeof meta>,
  positional: Positional<typeof meta>)` for standalone mains; inline mains
  (`new CLI('foo.ts', (opts, positional) => ..., meta)`) are contextually
  typed — no legacy `= {}` defaults, the engine always supplies argv.
  The first parameter is an assured **`Arguments` instance**
  (lib/runtime/CLI.ts): an Array subclass of the positionals with the
  parsed option values merged (`args.debug` works), plus `.parsed`
  (the `ParsedInvocation`), `.rawArgs`, `.opts`, `.has(flag)` (raw argv),
  `.help()`. `positional` is the plain array (legacy convenience)
- Return `exit(...)` — **never call `process.exit()` directly**:
    - `exit(0)` success · `exit(n)` fail with code n
    - `exit('explanation')` fail, message printed to stderr
    - `exit(err)` Error kind (`AbortError` → 130)
    - `exit(flow)` submodule kind — runs an Interface/TUI flow to completion
    - `exit(0, fn)` / `exit(n, fn)` — a bare function as the second argument
      is the **on-exit callback**: it runs during `complete()` before the
      process terminates (the happy-path form is `exit(0, fn)`)
- The Runtime (`lib/runtime/core.ts` run()/complete()) owns process
  termination; a main only returns signals

### Interactive work

- Gate: `runInteractively(fn)` bails with a `nonInteractive` ExitSignal
  when stdin is not a TTY — never construct Enquirer prompts unguarded
- TUI instances: `tui.confirm / input / select` member methods (enquirer
  loads lazily via `TUI.createInterface()`; `--help` bypasses the gate)
- Flows: `Interface.createInterface(name).stage(...)`; prompt factories
  `iface.confirm / input / select / query` produce thenable runnables —
  "return value" (`await`) or "return exit" (`exit(runnable)`)
- Effectful no-value steps in chains are plain function stages
  (`flow.stage(() => console.log(...))`) — there is deliberately no print
  factory

### Flows (TUI → TUI chains)

- Stage protocol dispatched by `exit()` kind: `exit(0)` advances;
  `exit('explanation')` / `exit(n)` terminate; plain values advance and
  chain as `prev`
- Stages are TUI submodules — see `test/interface.test.ts` for the pinned
  implementation

### Console streams

- `console.log` — program output, progress echoes, success markers
- `console.error` — errors, warnings, abort/die messages
- `console.dir` — structured object dumps

### Signals & abort

- `AbortError` is the canonical abort signal from prompts (ctrl-c/escape)
- Do not install `SIGINT`/`SIGHUP`/`SIGTERM` handlers or call
  `process.exit(130)` outside `lib/runtime/Module.ts` / `lib/runtime/core.ts`

### lib/ conventions

- One class per lib/ module (or one class + a few consuming methods); no
  standalone singleton objects in the export surface
- Import from the barrel: `import { Git } from '../lib/index.ts'`
- No single-consumer couples: code used by exactly one scripts/ module
  lives in that script, not in lib/

## Implementation Guidelines (for opencode sessions)

### Procedural Design & Sequential Structure in main()

When implementing a Rarebert system module's `main()` function:

1. **Entry point**: Function signature should be `async function main(args = [])`
2. **Sequential flow**: Each step should build on the previous, with clear state transitions
3. **Error handling**: Wrap critical sections in try/catch; log errors to stderr
4. **Command pattern**: Consider splitting into named subroutines if complexity > 50 lines

### Object-Oriented Datastructure Design

When designing data structures:

1. Prefer simple dicts/lists over full classes for scripts (simplicity)
2. Use objects with consistent keys/names across modules
3. Document the shape in docstrings or TypeScript annotations
4. For complex state, consider a `State` class at module level

### Declarative-Focused Implementation

When possible, favor declarative approaches:

1. **Config over code**: Let data drive behavior (JSON configs instead of if/else chains)
2. **Pure functions**: Make functions deterministic with no hidden state
3. **Immutable patterns**: Prefer creating new objects vs mutating existing ones
4. **Side effect isolation**: Keep I/O operations clearly separated

See `docs/modules.md` for the complete design language for CLI vs TUI modules and the elevation pattern.

### Git Operations via lib/git.ts

The `lib/git.ts` module provides a whitelisted git interface:

```javascript
import * as git from '../lib/git.ts';

// Stage all changes (safe wrapper)
git.add(['filename.js'], { all: true });

// Get status output
const status = git.git('status');
console.log(status.stdout); // stdout string
console.log(status.ok); // boolean success

// Create commit with message plan
git.git('commit', ['-m', 'formatted commit message']);
```

Use `git.git()` for any operation not directly wrapped. All operations are logged.

### Request Logging & Commit Message Instrumentation

Before commits, review the request history stored in `.last-module`:

1. The model receives `remember(name, content)` memos from previous failures/successes
2. When user makes direct requests, those statements accumulate as comments in module files
3. Check for `// REQUEST:` or `# TODO:` prefixes in source to understand intent
4. Use `bun launch.ts memo` to inject observations into implementation

### Model Capabilities by Provider/VRAM

- **WS-RAREBOX (24GB)**: Can run large quantization models, most flexible
- **WS-MINIFRIDGE (16GB)**: Good for mid-sized models, suitable for most tasks

The canonical provider keys and baseURLs live in `opencode.jsonc` — read it
before invoking `opencode run` (do not assume `localhost` or hardcode a host).
The model id format is `<provider>/<model>` where `<provider>` is a key under
`provider` in the config. Use `--model` to override the default, e.g.:

```
opencode run "<prompt>" -m ollama/laguna-xs-2.1:q8_0
```

### Analyze command

The `analyze` command (`scripts/analyze.ts` → `lib/introspect.ts` +
`lib/bindings.ts`) is the canonical source-map and dependency-tracing
tool. It is driven by polymorphic language primitives in
`lib/runtime/Language.ts`
(`lang*.js` support modules under `lib/supports/`), so JS/mjs/ts/py each
define their own parsing semantics. Below are the operational details an
agent should know before invoking it.

**Modes (mutually exclusive, in dispatch order):**

1. `--document` — opencode documentation pass (segment `main()`, document
   each block, optionally memoize). Requires a model; pass `--yes` to
   auto-memoize non-interactively.
2. `--trace <name>` — walk a binding's full dependency chain across modules.
3. `--graph` — print the resolved import graph (module list with counts).
4. default — condensed source-map summary per module (imports, declarations
   with 1-step resolution, exports).

**Module resolution:** `bun launch.ts analyze scripts/memo.ts` accepts
one or more paths (relPath, basename, or stem). With no args, launches a TUI
select over `listAllModules()`. Non-interactive stdin (piped) fails the
select — always pass module args in scripts/CI.

**Declarations are top-level, not just exported.** `extractTopLevelMembers`
captures every column-0 `const`/`let`/`var`/`function`/`class` declaration
with or without an `export` prefix. Non-exported decls are flagged
`exported: false` and rendered with a `, local` tag in the summary. This is
why `meta` and `main` (declared without `export`, re-exported via
`export default new CLI(...)`) appear in the declarations list. The older
`extractPublicMembers` is a back-compat filtered view (exported-only) and is
still used by `--document`'s fallback path.

**Import parsing handles multi-line blocks.** The gatherer caps continuation
at 200 lines and bails early if a new top-level statement begins before
`from` is found. A 19-line `import { ... } from '...'` block parses correctly.

**Tracing (`--trace`):** the `--trace` argument is a `::`-qualified path:

- `name` — find first module exporting/declaring `name`.
- `module::name` — resolve `name` in `module` (module may be a short name
  like `memo` → `lib/memo.ts`, a basename, or full relPath).
- `module::outer::inner` — **nested declaration tracing**: resolve `outer`
  as a top-level declaration, then descend into its body to find `inner` as
  a local declaration (via the language's `explorableMembers` map). The
  chain renders `outer` as `(function, ...)` and `inner` as
  `(local const, ...)`. Full recursion: the local's references are walked
  against sibling locals, module imports, and top-level declarations;
  imports recurse into their target module; cycles are detected via a
  `visited` set keyed by `${modPath}::${namePath}`.

**Pre-existing cycles in the import graph.** `lib/git.ts::git`,
`lib/module.ts::AbortError`, `lib/core.ts::store`, and
`lib/runtime/Project.ts::home` are mutually re-exported; traces that reach them
report `[cycle]` issues. This is expected, not a regression — the
cycle-detection prevents infinite recursion.

**Language parser caveats:**

- `lib/supports/lang*.js` files are ESM but have `.js` extensions, so
  `analyze` parses them with the CommonJS parser (`jsExtractBindings`),
  which looks for `require()` not `import`. These modules will show 0
  imports — their real ESM imports are not recognized. This is a known
  limitation of the `.js` extension mapping, not a bug in the module.
- The CommonJS parser only matches export/require patterns at column 0
  and skips comment lines, so template string values and JSDoc examples
  containing `require(...)` / `exports.x = ...` do not produce
  false-positive bindings.

**Verification recipe after editing `lib/introspect.ts` or any
`lang*.js`:** run `bun --print`-style syntax checks (or `bun scripts/bunliprobe.ts missing`)
on the touched files, then `bun launch.ts analyze scripts/<module>.ts`
(derive the expected import/declaration counts from the module's actual
source — the old pinned counts belonged to the now-removed
`scripts/commit.ts`), then `bun launch.ts analyze ... --trace <module>::main`
for the affected binding, then `bun launch.ts check`.

## Rarebert Specifications

### Signal handling & abort flow (ctrl-c / ctrl-d)

All process abort paths are centralized in `lib/runtime/Module.ts` (the
legacy `lib/cli.mjs` is gone). Do not install
`SIGINT`/`SIGHUP`/`SIGTERM` listeners or call `process.exit(130)` outside
that module.

- `installSignalHandlers()` is called once at startup in `launch.ts`. It
  registers a single handler for `SIGINT`, `SIGHUP`, `SIGTERM`, and
  `process.on('exit')` that runs every registered `onAbort` callback (in
  registration order) and then exits with code 130.
- `onAbort(callback)` registers a cleanup callback. Use it for any work
  that must run on abort (e.g. restoring the git index, flushing memos).
  Returns an unsubscribe function. `lib/memo.ts` registers `flush` this way.
- `AbortError` (exported from `lib/runtime/core.ts`) is the canonical way
  for a non-runtime module to signal an abort. Enquirer prompts reject on
  ctrl-c/escape — wrap `await prompt.run()` in try/catch and
  `throw new AbortError()` from the catch. The `run(meta, main)` wrapper
  catches it and calls `abort()` once, which prints `\nAborted.` to stderr,
  runs the cleanup callbacks, and exits 130.
- `die(message, code)` routes the message to `console.log` when
  `code === EXIT_OK` and to `console.error` otherwise. Always use `die()`
  for terminal exits instead of calling `process.exit()` directly with a
  manual print.

### Console output streams

- `console.log` — regular program output: progress echoes (`$ opencode ...`),
  success markers (`✓ Created ...`), banners, status lines (`ok ./mod`),
  non-interactive fallback notices that are not errors, section lists.
- `console.error` — true errors (`Failed to launch ...`,
  `git commit exited with status N`), warnings
  (`memo: performing a forgetful remember ...`), and abort/die messages
  routed through `lib/runtime/Module.ts`.
- `console.dir` — structured object dumps (used by `ok()`).

When in doubt, run `audit-consistency console-streams` to verify.

### Consistency audits

The `audit-consistency` skill (`.opencode/skills/audit-consistency/SKILL.md`)
exercises `bun launch.ts check` and `bun launch.ts edit` non-interactively to
verify a named
topic across the codebase. Invoke it as `audit-consistency {topic}` with one
of: `console-streams`, `signal-handling`, `abort-flow`, `naming`. See the
skill body for the per-topic rules.

### Brainstorm Pattern for Complex Tasks

The `brainstorm` skill (`.opencode/skills/brainstorm/SKILL.md`) provides
a strategy for complex multi-step tasks that requires both cloud and local
model capabilities:

1. **Plan with cloud**: Submit a planning workload to a cloud model via task
   subagent. The model analyzes and returns structured JSON with todos and
   exact code snippets.
2. **Create todos**: Parse the planning response and create todo items using
   the `todowrite` tool.
3. **Implement locally**: Execute each todo using a local quantized model
   via `opencode run`, with the agent orchestrating the flow.

This pattern supersedes `delegate` by using expensive cloud credits only
for reasoning (planning), while cheaper local models handle implementation.

**Key difference from delegate:**

- Delegate: subagent → cloud model → implementation
- Brainstorm: subagent → cloud model (for PLAN ONLY) → agent → local model (for implementation)

## Unfinished Work

### Exit-handling migration (lib/ only — scripts/ layer superseded)

The `exit()` helper (`lib/runtime/core.ts`) is the canonical termination path
for `CLI` main callbacks: it routes through `Module.exit()` so signal
handlers and `onAbort` cleanup callbacks (memo flush, git-index restore)
run before the process ends.

**Superseded 2026-10-23:** the `scripts/` layer items (article, run, trail)
are gone — the modules were removed/stubbed in the Bunli slim-down and
`lib/run.mjs`/`lib/article.mjs`/`lib/present.mjs` no longer exist.

**`lib/` layer — `process.exit()` in library code (remaining):**

Library functions that terminate the process directly cannot be intercepted
by the caller. Migration requires changing them to return error codes or
throw `AbortError`, letting the script's `CLI` wrapper call `exit()`.

| File             | Lines    | Context                        |
| ---------------- | -------- | ------------------------------ |
| `lib/opencode.ts`| spawn-failure path | resurface as AbortError |
| `lib/ide.ts`     | editor-launch failure | resurface as AbortError |
| `lib/backend.ts` | non-interactive config failure | resurface as AbortError |
| `lib/server.ts`  | 133–135  | ping probe — intentional, leave |

Each migration should be followed by `bun test` and a manual exercise of the
affected command.

### Repo typecheck gate (tools/typescript is installed; no passing scope yet)

`tsc --noEmit` over the repo currently reports ~450 errors, ALL in legacy
files — the typed-arguments surface (lib/runtime/CLI.ts, TUI parameter
seam, all scripts metas/mains, test/typed-args.test.ts) is at **zero**
errors under `--module nodenext --allowImportingTsExtensions
--esModuleInterop`. Breakdown of the legacy debt (non-strict tsc):

- `lib/runtime/core.ts` (79) + `lib/runtime/Project.ts` (35) — stale
  interface shapes: `ExitSignal` lacks the `code/onExit/retry/cleanup/
  submodule/error` fields the machinery reads/writes; `ProjectFolder` /
  `Project` lack `key/rel/dir/label/exts/root`. Completing those
  interfaces likely clears all ~114 and unblocks a `lib/runtime` scope.
- `lib/introspect.ts` (123), `lib/server.ts` (93), `lib/memo.ts` (39),
  `lib/editor.ts` (25), `lib/backend.ts` (22) — historical implicit-any
  helpers and union-vs-property mismatches.
- Because `core.ts` is transitively imported by every runtime file, ANY
  tsc program that includes the typed seam drags `core.ts` in — a passing
  scoped gate is impossible until the `ExitSignal` interface is completed.
  No `typecheck` package.json script exists for this reason; add one once
  the two interface files are cleaned.
